question: Why is even immense material wealth insufficient compared to possessing this teaching?
premises: An ocean filled with jewels represents vast wealth
Such accumulation may belong to someone
The comparison implies the teaching surpasses it
inference: Even one who could fill the ocean with jewels lacks an equivalent to this teaching.
uncertainties: The form akretuṃ is irregular and its exact grammatical analysis is uncertain
plain_english: Even if one had the wealth to fill the ocean with jewels.
